description.narrative:
Gender Justice
a. Violence against women and girls is eliminated b. Policies and practices protect the equal rights of women, girls c. Women are in leadership positions across different sectors
Accountable governance a. Feminist and youth movements are adequately supported and resourced. Transformative public education systems empower young people, especially girls.
Program Goal for GenderJustice is; Diverse women, girls, and marginalised groups fully realise their rights, exercise their leadership, and live a life free from violence, discrimination, and poverty.
Strategic Objective 1: Women, girls, and marginalised groups in SAF live free from violence in both their private and public lives.
1.1 Women, including young women, influence decisions on policies, programmes, and resources to end VAWG including ending impunity for perpetrators.
· Promote domestication and popularization of the SADC GBV modellaw and SADC Ending Child Marriage Law in All 4 countries through research and advocacy on fulfilment of national law gaps · Support Ending violence against women and girls (EVAWG) campaign in Malawi, Damba Kurembera Sandi Kuibva in Zimbabwe, CHEGA in Mozambique and I Can in Zambia. · Work with feminist movements- Women Manifesto Movement, Women Human Rights Defenders, NGO CC, Women’s Observatory, Musasa to advance women's rights issues including challenging social norm, ending Impunity. · Work with Women’s Rights Organisation (WROs) and Youth-Led Organisation (YLOs) to gather evidence at community and district levels for use to influence polices, programmes and resources to end EVAWG.
1.2 Increased availability, accessibility, and utilization of GBV essential services
· Workingwith the Parliamentary Women Caucuses in all countries to advocate for increased resources allocation to GBV essential services. · Capacity building to GBV essential services providers including the Police, Judiciary in Malawi. · Support community level referralssystems for GBV essential services in Malawi, Mozambique and Zambia. · Raise awareness on the available GBV services in the communities in Chibombo, Chisamba, Itezhi-tezhi and Namwala of Zambia · Capacity building for health providers on GBV to identify, attend to and refer cases to the police in Mozambique. · Capacity strengthening of health providers in gender sensitive services including GBV services at community level in Zambia. · Train community members and other influential people to identify and refer cases of GBV in Mozambique. · Advocate to improve the follow-up of community GBV cases by the police in Mozambique. · Provision of mobile one stop centers and safe space activities enabling convenient access and relevant services particularly sexual reproductive health services. · Strengthening of essential services in certain districts in Zimbabwe which had no dedicated Police Victim Friendly Unit (VFU) offices, for survivors of GBV, reducing distances survivors would ordinarily walk to access essential services. · Development of an app by a partner (Musasa) with support from Oxfam in Zimbabwe that created a free text it chat-box enabling vulnerable communities toaccess GBV essential information and services at the click of a button, innovation greatly appreciated by rights holders
1.3: Positive shifts in socio norms and harmful masculinities for ending VAWG
· Support learning and development of a strategy on Ending Child Marriages in all four countries · Addressing social norms to encourage men and boys to participate in EVAWG in all four countriesthrough the Enough Campaign in Zimbabwe/Chega in Mozambique. · Engage at least 12 male MPs in bilateral meetings in six constituencies, raising awareness on the unequal distribution of UCDW during ministerial the question time in Parliament. · Support MPs to raise questions during the impending debate on the Marriage Amendment Bill to ignite conversations on UCDW, and linkages of payment of lobola (the bride price) underpinned men’s entitlement to relegating women and girls to perform UCDW as part of the marriage institution. · Present position paper through Padare Men’s Forum on Gender to Parliamentary Thematic Committees and Portfolio Committees on the Policy Score Card (PSC) to engender buy in on the use of the PSC tool to measure Government commitment on UCDW · Capacity building of men and boys through in gender transformative approaches through partner Men for Gender Equality Now (MEGEN) in Malawi · Working with traditional leaders/male champions to shift negative social norms towards women leadership including political leadership inMalawi. · Conduct social media campaigns on social norms and positive masculinity in Zambia · Engage community leaders and norm-setters to promote positive shifts in socio norms and promote women’s rights to end VAWG in Malawi, Zambia, Zimbabwe and Mozambique · Strengthen the capacities of men and boys in terms of social norms and make them allies and defenders of women's rights in Mozambique 1.4: Increased agency among victims and survivors of VAWG on their rights
· Work with women including young women for increased agency, exercise their rights and shape decisions in all levels of social economic and political spheres in Malawi and Zimbabwe. · Working with Malawi Police Service, Judiciary and Social Welfare to support survivors of violence to access justice. · Support survivors of VAWG with safe spaces and shelters · Identification, referral of survivors to health facilities and follow-up with beneficiaries in Mozambique · Ensure that gender statistics are available including GBV data through women barometer in Mozambique Strategic Objective 2: Diverse women, including young women, have full agency, exercise their rights, and shape decisions in all levels of social, economic, and political life.
2.1 Women, including young women, movements, networks, and their organisations effectively participate in governance processes including elections
· Support to the Women Parliament Caucus in Malawi in development of strategic plan. · Support Women Parliamentary Caucus in Zambia to implement their strategic plan · Support partners (WCoZ) and (WALPE) to run the 50/50 advocacy campaign influencing Government of Zimbabwe, public institutions, and political parties to fulfil Section 56 of theZimbabwe Constitution, calling for equal opportunities in all socio-economic spheres. · Campaign culminated in partners meeting First Lady in a closed meeting advocating for implementation Section 56 in Zimbabwe, · Conduct Capacity building in Women’s transformational leadership, engagement with media etc to Parliamentary Women Caucuses of Malawi, Zambia and Zimbabwe; · Provide postelection support to the Parliamentary Women’s Caucus in Zimbabwe on joint collaboration on general campaigns · Work with the Girls Gone Political, a youth movement to support and promote young women to participate in governance processes and elections at all levels in Zambia. · Support cluster learning on women and governance. · Work women and young women and marginalised groups in promoting women political leadership in Malawi especially towards 2025 elections. · Support Ministry of Gender in Malawi to review the Political Empowerment of Women Strategy and support their convening role in engaging political parties for gender transformation. · Conduct media-based campaigns on women, young women participation in 2025 elections · Increased participation, leadership and influence of women in community-level, national and international climate change negotiations (Malawi and Mozambique). · Partners and support the National Women Observatory in efforts to build Female Parliamentarians at all levels in Mozambique
2.2 Women’s rights movements, organisations have improved and sustainable resources and capacities to collectively drive change on women’s leadership
· Provide economic support to women's rights and feminist movements to collectively advance women's leadership in Malawi. · Collaboration with other development partners and CSOs for mobilisation of resources for CSOs and WRO for engagement in elections in Malawi with a focus on increasing women and youth participation in Politics. · Support the women’s rights movement to strengthen their advocacy interventions through thought leadership on women’s rights issues in Zambia. · Jointly mobilise resources with the women’s movements and organisations for programming for women’s leadership through fundraising. · Strengthen the capacity of women to take up leadership through trainings and mentorship is leadership hubs in selected districts of Zambia. · Support women’s groups with livelihoods though farmer fields schools in In Zambia. · Increased involvement by women and youth in budget influencing in Zomba District in Malawi and Chokwe District in Mozambique
2.3 Women, including young women, and their movements, organisations, and allies, influence positive changes in socio norms and formal institutions in support of women’s leadership.
· Profiling of women in political leadership in Malawi and Zambia · Using women movements through the Gender transformative resilience initiatives for Malawi and Mozambique to influence gender transformation in the district councils in Zomba in Malawi and Chokwe in Mozambique · Engage political leadership on deliberate actions and strategies to promote women in leadership positions in Malawi, Zambia and Zimbabwe Strategic Objective 3: Women, includingyoung women, enjoy their rights to control and benefit from resources, assets, income and their own time, and their paid and unpaidwork is valued in SAF societies and economies.
3.1 Women, including young women, and their movements influence decision-makers fordevelopment and implementation of gender-responsive economic policies.
· Support Adolescent Girls and young women with economic empowerment activities through HFHC program in Malawi, Mozambique and Zambia. · Support climate smart businesses under Gender transformative resilience initiatives for Malawi and Mozambique under the African Development Bank Funding · Working with Women’s Coalition of Zimbabwe building effective advocacy in WEE- Zimbabwe targeting parliament. · Enhance resilience and sustainability and graduate rural households, including women and the youth from ultra-poverty in Malawi under Flanders and Irish Aid funding streams · Support transition of women and girls to vocational training for economic resilience through program with Irish Aid in Malawi
3.2 Increasedgender responsive budgeting
· Support budget analysis for increased budget allocation for Gender and SRHR commodities. · Supporting local government institutions to develop gender responsive frameworks to ensure gender responsive budgeting in Malawi through the women and politics project funded by the EU project in Malawi. · Mobilising women and youth to participate during the national budget consultation and public hearings at national and local level in all countries. · Collaborate with University of Zimbabwe and UN Women in engaging Parliament of Zimbabwe and develop a policy brief Post-2022 National Budget Statement and highlight the lack of women’s voices and agency in setting women’s priorities with regards to the sharing of the national budget. · Policy brief will recommend to the Government of Zimbabwe implementation of a gender responsive budget (GRB) to increase investment in care work policies, infrastructure and care related services to address the social and political inequalities faced by women and girls; · Supported grassroots women to participate in national budget consultations across 8 centres in Zimbabwe (4 urban <(>&<)> 4 rural).
3.3 Increased adoption of UCDW policies and practices by national and local authorities in SAF
• Undertaking a multi-country study together with partners (Padare included) looking at understanding the frames that different audiences (such as traditional and religious leaders) hold on unpaid care, informal work, and the economy, and identifying which types of frames and narratives on these issues are most compelling, why, and how to make them work with different audiences. To be led by Zimbabwe • Shifting narratives and challenging the negative masculinity that fuel the workload of UCDW in Zimbabwe. • Influencing policy makers to ensure that policies are enacted to address the unequal distribution of UCDW in Zimbabwe. • Forge alliances with relevant duty bearers (Memorandum of Understanding with Parliamentary Portfolio Committees PPC Secretariat) - Zimbabwe; • Conduct a study on time use with Ministry of Labour in Zambia on valuing women’s work. • Raise awareness on valuing women’s work through dissemination of the time-use on valuing women’s work report atthe national level and Western and Southern Provinces of Zambia. • Follow up on the partner led petitioning to Parliament of Zimbabwe’s public hearing on the recognition of unpaid care and domestic work as an economic and public policy issue and work with Parliament to have a national care policy on UCDW. • Support We Care partner (Bekezela) to engage policy makers from Bubi Rural District Council and chairperson of the District Water Supply and Sanitation Committee (DWSSC) to prioritise women’s need to access water and health services through use of national devolution funds to expand solarised piped water schemes (PWS) to reach more households in the district.
Strategic Objective 4: Women, girls, and marginalized groups in SAF are able to fully exercise and enjoy their sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR).
4.1 Women, including young women, influence decisions on policies, programmes, and resources to realize SRHR
• Engage ministries, government agencies, Parliamentarians and Council Leaders, journalist on SRHR existing gaps, on law reforms and SRHR resource allocation at national level in Malawi, Zambia and Mozambique • Strengthen the capacity and alliance of WROs on SRHR in Malawi, Zambia and Mozambique • Engage ministries, government agencies create safe and friendly spaces (for women, girls, persons of diverse SOGIEC, boys and men to share information on safe abortion and post abortion care, comprehensive sexuality education and comprehensive contraception care services available in their communities in Mozambique. • Campaigns focused onSRHR related social norm change and available SRH services organized in communities in Malawi, Mozambique and Zambia
4.2 Systems deliver quality comprehensive SRHR essential services
• Strengthen the supply systems of key SRHR commodities at health facilities in Malawi, Mozambique and Zambia • Strengthen health service providers capacity on gender-responsive SRH services focused on comprehensive abortion care, post-abortion care, self-managed abortion, post abortion and contraception in Malawi, Mozambique and Zambia. •Strengthen Health systems including remote and technological based solutions for youth friendly services in Malawi, Zambia and Mozambique. • Strengthen health care provider capacity to provide LGBT community members friendly services in Mozambique. • Provide Technical assistance on health information systems and policy outreach to health service facilities in Mozambique • Provide technical assistance on management of SRH services and gender-sensitive spaces to health facilities in Mozambique • Develop or adapt existing communications strategies on positive norm modelling for SRHR and SGBV prevention and LGBTQI rights in Mozambique.
4.3 Increased agency among young people, WROs and YLOs to demand SRHR
• Strengthen engagement of Women Rights Organizations and Youth Led Organizations in advocating for policies and resources to support SRHR at the national – regional (Southern Africa) and international level inMalawi, Zambia and Mozambique • Strengthen capacity of WROs and YLOs to engage stakeholders and advocate for effective implementation of SRHR policies and laws at different levels (at national and regional level) in Malawi, Zambia and Mozambique. • Capacity building adolescent girls and young women to demand SRHR among their families and communities in Mozambique, Malawi and Zambia • Increaseknowledge of SRHR among adolescent girls and young women so that they can freely decide on their SRHR rights in Mozambique, Malawi and Zambia • Develop program and guide for dialogue on SGBV prevention and SRHR in Zambia, Mozambique and Malawi
Strategic Objective 5: Girls and other Vulnerable Children attain equitable and transformative education opportunities in terms of enrolment, participation, retention, and completion at all levels.
5.1 Increased investments and accountability in delivery of transformative and quality education by governments in Southern Africa
· Conduct Budget Analysis of the National Education Budget and use findings to lobby for increased resource allocations to National Education budget in Malawi. · Collaborate with Female Members of Parliament and targeted Law Makers to influence and lobby for resource allocations to Education in Malawi · Engage with the national and provincial Diretorates to demand for increase of the National Education Budget and increased resource allocations to National Education budget inMozambique · Collaborate with Female Members of Parliament and targeted Law Makers to influence and lobby for resource allocations to Education in Mozambique
5.2 Government, CSOs and Local Communities create systems for safe schools and learning for girls and boys
· Create a safe learning environment for learners by challenging negative socio norms that affect girls’ education through awareness campaigns in Malawi, Mozambique and Zimbabwe · Improve enrolment, retention, and completion of learners in targeted schools through provision of bursaries, bicycles, school materials and construction of girl friendly infrastructures in Malawi and Zimbabwe · Conduct non-formal education for young girls and boys at targeted communities · Enhance community and school structures capabilitiesto address school gender-based violence and promote girls’ education in Malawi, Mozambique and Zimbabwe · Improve access to safe girl-friendly sanitation infrastructures and hygiene in rural school in Mozambique, Malawi and Zimbabwe
5.3 Civil society Organisations, citizens and local communities have increased voice and action in demand for delivery of quality education as an essential service.
▫ Enhance local partner and Civil Society Platform to Conduct Budget Analysis of the National Education Budget and use findings to lobby for increased resource allocations to National Education budget in Mozambique Build active citizenship of communities oninfluencing school improvement grants ( SIG’s ) in Phlombe, Mulanje and Balaka in Malawi

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education forall, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam established this country office to support local organizations and projects. Through this local office Oxfam Novib directly contributes towards this project’s implementation.
